media.transcript: Some professional GeoGuessr players have started using the positions of the moon and the planets in the sky to determine where they are. Let me explain. So some countries, like the United Kingdom, have extremely dense street view. The red lines on this map represent everywhere the Google car has been. Contrast this with the African country of Botswana, where only the main roads have Google coverage. In addition to this, all the Botswana coverage was actually done in mid-2012, meaning it's been in GeoGuessr ever since GeoGuessr came out. And so people, such as the Norwegian Geoguesser Pro Havard, have studied the roads of Botswana meticulously, and realized that when the Google car drove the A2 highway in June 2012, the moon was to the northwest of the car in the sky. You can see this if you zoom in all the way, and it can actually help you distinguish this road. What's even crazier is that on the highway A35, if you zoom in just over the tree canopy to the east, you can see Venus, and it follows you along for pretty much the whole road, leading to very close guesses.

media.transcript: I plan my psychotically long walks for tools that I use to make sure that they are the best they can possibly be. We start off with Google Maps. Pick two locations at the streets so that I know what to expect and that it's going to be an aesthetically pleasing, overall pleasing experience because you can go from point A to point B. It can be a really awesome experience or it can be a horrible experience really depending on the route that you take. VEA. I organize my walks. I'm out and about on any given day. Photos of things that I want to revisit. Save them in VEA and then I'll go back when I'm planning my walks to pinpoint the things that I have saved as places to stop or pass. Favorite feature is that you can take a photo, a live photo in the app and it saves it, geolocates it and categorizes it in the app for you. I love this because so many times when I'm on my walks, I'll take a photo of something and be like, oh my god, I have to come back to this and then it gets lost in the void of my camera roll. VEA, I take the photo, it automatically saves it and I know exactly where it is. Use it and save their locations. Inspo for where I should stop, places that are good to stop, and like bounce ideas off each other. So you can save locations from Google Maps directly into VEA. Find a taco place that I really want to stop at. I can find it on Google Maps, save it to VEA and then it's in my folder of places I want to stop. Klema. When I start my walks, I block all social media with Klema. The whole point of these walks is to connect the external world, to be in the present, to decompress and get away from things that make you anxious like social media. Forcibly blocks you out of the app. If you try to go to it, it says no, no, no. We love her. Next is Apple Podcasts, Spotify or Libby. I want to optimize these walks to be the most beneficial they possibly can. Either do silence or one of these podcasts or educational videos. Cool, you can start your walk and by the end of it, you're super educated about some random topic or discipline. So if I'm not listening to a podcast or just literally like contemplating life, I'm on the phone with my mother, my sister or my cousin. These are the tools and apps that I use to make my walks the best that they can possibly be. I hope that this was helpful and you guys will take your own psychologically long walk. Bye.
